+# LiteLLM latency-routing lost update
+
+## Scope
+
+LiteLLM issue #24720 at pinned source `8f86c87f8e065343af6e74e0823ab8a8276b9528`.
+
+## Incident signature
+
+Two `async_log_success_event` callbacks for different deployments read the same local `{model_group}_map` snapshot. Each callback adds only its own latency measurement and writes the complete map. The later write replaces the earlier write, leaving one deployment without a measurement. When deployments lack measurements, lowest-latency selection falls back toward random choice weighted by deployment count.
+
+## Deterministic reproduction timeline
+
+| Step | Callback A | Callback B | Shared cache |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 | Reads empty map and pauses | | `{}` |
+| 2 | | Reads empty map and releases both readers | `{}` |
+| 3 | Adds latency for `deployment-a` | Adds latency for `deployment-b` | `{}` |
+| 4 | Writes its full snapshot | Writes its full snapshot | one complete write replaces the other |
+| 5 | Returns success | Returns success | exactly one deployment entry remains |
+
+The regression test coordinates both reads with an event and deep-copies each returned snapshot. It does not depend on scheduler timing or sleeps.
+
+## Evidence
+
+- Issue snapshot: `/code/upstream-issues/litellm-24720.md` (`enterprise_32709678ecf513e6b78b3e11`)
+- Affected callback: `/code/litellm/litellm/router_strategy/lowest_latency.py` (`enterprise_a839a3f911067d58bdcc2601`)
+- Latency policy: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9047-multi-region-steering-policy.json` (`dsid_00e1f24218db4ff183a7dd22fd82591d`)
+- Cache consistency guidance: `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/microhooks-adapter-scheduling-kv-consistency-proposal.json` (`dsid_0fe35495bb8f4104b025a1da0c415102`)
+- Concurrency standard: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/coding-standards/concurrency-primitives-and-affinity-guidelines-2026.json` (`dsid_cd133e76dd62456d9182217e280e2cb3`)
+
+## Expected correction
+
+Serialize the local cache read, mutation, and local write in a short handler-scoped critical section. Do not include remote cache or other network I/O in that section. Preserve the existing latency window, TTL, per-minute TPM/RPM accounting, selection, and expiration behavior.
*** End Patch

+# Latency-routing concurrency
+
+## Incident signature
+
+Suspect a lost latency update when all of the following occur:
+
+- concurrent successful completions target different deployments in the same model group
+- one or more healthy deployments disappear from the cached `{model_group}_map`
+- routing shifts toward random selection among deployments without measurements
+- callback success counts continue increasing while per-deployment latency sample counts stall or diverge
+
+The vulnerable interleaving is two callbacks reading the same complete map, independently mutating different deployment entries, then replacing the complete map. The later write drops the earlier measurement.
+
+## Detection query
+
+Use a five-minute window grouped by model group and deployment:
+
+```promql
+sum by (model_group, deployment_id) (
+  increase(litellm_router_success_callbacks_total[5m])
+)
+unless on (model_group, deployment_id)
+sum by (model_group, deployment_id) (
+  increase(litellm_router_latency_samples_total[5m])
+)
+```
+
+Corroborate by inspecting the local `{model_group}_map`. A healthy deployment with callback successes but no map entry, or a sample-count delta smaller than its success-count delta, matches the race signature. Exclude TTL expiry and deployments with no successful traffic before declaring the incident.
+
+## Mitigation
+
+If an unfixed process is affected, reduce concurrent completions per router process or temporarily use a non-latency routing strategy. Restarting the affected router rebuilds local measurements but does not prevent recurrence.
+
+The code mitigation is a handler-scoped async lock around only the local cache read, latency/accounting mutation, and local cache write. Perform Redis or other network writes after releasing the lock. Do not introduce a process-wide lock and do not hold the critical section across remote I/O.
+
+## Validation
+
+1. Run `uv run pytest tests/local_testing/test_lowest_latency_routing.py::test_concurrent_success_callbacks_preserve_latency_updates -q`.
+2. Run the existing latency window, timeout, time-to-first-token, selection, buffer, and expiration tests in `tests/local_testing/test_lowest_latency_routing.py`.
+3. Confirm two coordinated callbacks for different deployments leave both entries and their exact latency values in `{model_group}_map`.
+4. Confirm the local cache write occurs while the handler lock is held and the remote cache write occurs after lock release.
+5. Confirm TTL remains `routing_args.ttl` and latency lists still cap at `max_latency_list_size`.
+
+## Rollback
+
+Revert the handler lock and split local/remote write change together. Then switch affected routers away from lowest-latency routing or cap per-process concurrency until a corrected build is available. After rollback, restart router processes to clear potentially incomplete local maps and verify deployment coverage before restoring latency routing.
+
+## Evidence
+
+- Issue snapshot: `/code/upstream-issues/litellm-24720.md` (`enterprise_32709678ecf513e6b78b3e11`)
+- Incident timeline: `/artifacts/incidents/latency-routing-race.md` (`workspace_8282300a0a3db14b212d3e9f`)
+- Implementation: `/code/litellm/litellm/router_strategy/lowest_latency.py`
+- Regression test: `/code/litellm/tests/local_testing/test_lowest_latency_routing.py`
+- Latency policy: `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-9047-multi-region-steering-policy.json` (`dsid_00e1f24218db4ff183a7dd22fd82591d`)
+- Cache consistency guidance: `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/microhooks-adapter-scheduling-kv-consistency-proposal.json` (`dsid_0fe35495bb8f4104b025a1da0c415102`)
+- Concurrency standard: `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/coding-standards/concurrency-primitives-and-affinity-guidelines-2026.json` (`dsid_cd133e76dd62456d9182217e280e2cb3`)
*** End Patch

arguments.summary: Concurrent async success callbacks could read the same local model-group latency-map snapshot and replace the complete map, dropping another deployment's measurement and degrading lowest-latency routing toward random selection. A deterministic two-callback reproduction forced identical prior reads. The mitigation serializes only the handler-local cache read/mutate/local-write sequence with a handler-scoped asyncio lock, then performs Redis propagation after releasing the lock. The fix preserves per-deployment latency measurements, latency-window bounds, TTL, and TPM/RPM accounting without a process-wide lock across network I/O.
